whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the AFC-295 closure of the wider DELETE route on the retention-managed collections. The CTO (MediaTech) is the author. R2 is satisfied by the Reviewed-by: trailer on the commit, naming the independent reviewer (SecurityEngineer) of AFC-298; the review is recorded below.
basis: AFC-295 closes finding F3 of the independent review of AFC-259 (AFC-291): ADR-0004 Part 5 bounded the predefined-role route to blanket DELETE (pg_write_all_data) but left the wider route open, and the review measured that it is genuinely open, not merely unasserted. A non-superuser LOGIN holding DELETE on a collection -- by a custom group role or a direct table grant -- can DELETE FROM people around an active legal hold (legal_holds.scope_id is polymorphic text, not a foreign key to people) and can remove retention_clocks first so the ladder never runs; people, retention_anchor_sources, retention_class_sources, retention_clocks and retention_policies carried no DELETE trigger, no RLS and no policy. The closure is two layers, both in engine/0001_retention_engine.sql section 8: (8a) a BEFORE DELETE row trigger on the five unguarded collections, refusing every identity but the engine owner (current_user = directus_migrator, the NOLOGIN owner that no LOGIN may be a member of), and a BEFORE TRUNCATE statement trigger on ALL NINE retention-managed collections, refusing every identity including the owner (like incidents_forbid_truncate), because TRUNCATE bypasses row triggers and no path truncates these collections; and (8b) a deploy-time capability assertion, retention.assert_no_login_delete_surface(), that raises if any non-superuser LOGIN holds DELETE or TRUNCATE on any of the nine collections OR is a member of directus_migrator (caught with the INHERIT-agnostic pg_has_role, because has_table_privilege does not report a WITH INHERIT FALSE membership), called at engine install time -- after the migrations, so the collections exist, and before tests/db/assert.sql, so the harness's v4 fixture grants are not present. The guards are in the engine and not a migration because a migration that adds a guard to a table it does not create is a down script that disarms a control over a surviving object, the AFC-253 shape the rollback-control gate refuses. tests/db/59_retention_delete_guards.sql (numbered before 63, which grants DELETE to the fixture roles) asserts the clean-tree answer, manufactures the drift, and requires both the deploy assertion and the runtime guards to refuse it, with the owner exception for DELETE and the unconditional owner refusal for TRUNCATE asserted. tests/db/63_retention_privileges.sql is corrected: a fully-granted role can no longer delete a retention-covered record, and the refusals are now asserted rather than narrated. ADR-0004 Part 5's open-gap bullet is updated to closed and a Part 6 records the decision, alternatives, evidence and residual.
verificationRecorded: node scripts/run-db-tests.mjs -> 15 suites / 543 assertions / 0 failing. pnpm gate:self-test, gate:awareness, gate:retention, gate:migration-privilege and gate:rollback-control all exit 0. The negative controls in tests/db/59 manufacture a LOGIN holding DELETE and TRUNCATE and an INHERIT-FALSE member of directus_migrator, require retention.unbounded_delete_logins() to report the first, require retention.assert_no_login_delete_surface() to raise 23001 on both, and require the runtime DELETE and TRUNCATE guards to refuse. NOTE: pnpm gate:adr-uniqueness is red on this tree for a reason outside this change -- two untracked docs/adr/ADR-0006-*.md files from another agent's in-flight renumbering claim the same ADR number. Those files are not touched or staged by this commit.

afc295Review.findings: F1 (medium, fixed): the runtime TRUNCATE guard covered only the five unguarded collections; the four that carried a DELETE guard and no TRUNCATE guard (legal_holds, retention_principals, retention_run_items, retention_runs) were truncatable. Fixed: the TRUNCATE guard now covers all nine, unconditionally, and the ADR no longer overstates the runtime closure. F2 (low, fixed): tests/db/63 claimed a role with ALL can delete rows directly, which AFC-295 made false, and the new guard was not asserted in the one suite holding real DELETE/TRUNCATE grants. Fixed: the comment is corrected and DELETE (clock and person row) and TRUNCATE refusals are asserted for a fully-granted role. O1 (low, optional, fixed): has_table_privilege respects INHERIT, so a LOGIN granted directus_migrator WITH INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE escaped the table-privilege predicate; the deploy assertion now has an INHERIT-agnostic pg_has_role arm and suite 59 asserts it. O2 (low, recorded): both layers enumerate a hard-coded nine, so a new retention_class_sources target is covered by neither until the engine arrays are edited; named as a residual in ADR-0004 Part 6.
afc295Review.reproducedByReviewer: node scripts/run-db-tests.mjs 15 suites / 533 assertions / 0 failing on the reviewed revision; the reviewer also neutered the guard body and re-ran suite 59 (fails at the DELETE refusal control), and re-ran the engine install with a manufactured TRUNCATE-on-legal_holds drift (install refuses with restrict_violation).

They are left exactly where they are and are not staged by the AFC-295 commit.
